contexts: 190-bed children's hospital, about 620 asthma admissions a year
five-section paper plan scanned into the chart
reading: A complete plan sits between the admission and the 90 days at home, but so do severity, previous admissions, controller medicine and family circumstances, which also shape who gets a complete plan. Revisits are only fully visible through provincial linkage because one in five happens elsewhere, most often for lower-income families. Language preference affects whether a complete plan is usable. The measurement tool exists; the missing piece is a linked, adjusted comparison in this hospital's population.

summary: Map places plan completeness among the confounders that also decide who revisits, and shows why linkage is needed to count the outcome.
